item.vhs.name: Cursed VHS
item.vhs.description: An old unlabeled VHS tape. No sender name, and the rewind button seems stuck. It looks like it belongs in the tape deck on the farmhouse TV.
item.pencil.name: Pencil
item.pencil.description: An ordinary HB pencil. There really shouldn't be anything frightening about it.
item.cabinet.name: Occult Cabinet
item.cabinet.description: A wooden cabinet covered in occult markings. It can temporarily seal the anchor of an entity attached to you.
story.vhs.origin-package: The next morning, a brown-paper parcel is waiting outside your door.^No stamp. No sender.^Inside is only an old VHS tape and a handwritten note:^‘DO NOT REWIND.’^On one corner of the label, the number ‘18’ was written in pencil... then almost completely erased.
story.vhs.parcel-spotted: A strange brown-paper parcel is sitting beside your front door...
story.vhs.parcel-action: Move closer and inspect the parcel.
story.vhs.received: You received an old VHS tape.^It looks like it should go into the tape deck on the TV inside the farmhouse.
story.vhs.install: *Click.* The VHS disappears into the TV. The eject button does not respond.
story.vhs.signal-repeat: The TV crackles, then cuts out. Sudoku is standing beside you.
story.vhs.inventory-full: Your inventory is full. Leave an empty slot to receive the VHS tape.
npc.dialogue.mon: Don't touch the tape.$2#$b#...I haven't finished solving it.
npc.dialogue.tue: The number 7 can't appear twice in the same row.$2#$b#How many times have I told you that?
npc.dialogue.wed: You keep looking at me as though I crawled out of the TV.$2
npc.dialogue.thu: I'm not haunting your house.$2#$b#I'm just... here.
npc.dialogue.fri: If the screen turns on by itself, don't unplug it.$2#$b#It's irritating.
npc.dialogue.sat: People call this the weekend?$2#$b#I call it time to solve a 9x9 grid.
npc.dialogue.sun: ......$2#$b#I don't have anything frightening to say today.
npc.dialogue.rainy.0: Rain makes the screen noisier.$2#$b#I like it.
npc.dialogue.rainy.1: If you hear water dripping from the TV... ignore it.$2
npc.dialogue.indoor.0: Do you have a pencil yet?$2
npc.dialogue.indoor.1: I'm thinking about an empty cell.$2#$b#Don't bother me.

intro.pencil.warning.hoe.1: Sudoku looks at the hoe. Then at you.
intro.pencil.warning.hoe.2: ‘...Do you not want to live anymore?’
intro.pencil.warning.hoe.3: ‘I need a pencil. A. Pencil. Stop pointing that thing at the board.’
intro.pencil.warning.missing.1: Sudoku stares at your empty hands for a long moment.
intro.pencil.warning.missing.2: ‘...Do you not want to live anymore?’
intro.pencil.warning.missing.3: ‘I need a pencil. Bring me one and come back. I'll wait.’
intro.pencil.warning.question: Sudoku folds her arms. She clearly isn't negotiating.
story.player-thought.pencil-shop: A pencil... Pierre probably sells those.
story.prologue.invitation.first: This morning, you find a note slipped under the door.^‘Everyone's getting together at the Stardrop Saloon tonight. Come by around 6 PM! — Gus’^It sounds like they're expecting you.
story.prologue.invitation.reminder: Another note arrives from the Stardrop Saloon.^‘Didn't see you yesterday. Everyone will be around again tonight at about 6 PM. Stop by if you can! — Gus’
story.prologue.hud.1730: The gathering at the Stardrop Saloon will start soon...
story.prologue.hud.1800: Everyone is probably at the Stardrop Saloon by now.
story.prologue.saloon.header: A Gathering at the Stardrop Saloon
story.prologue.saloon.gus.1: Oh, you made it! Make yourself comfortable. Nothing serious tonight — just drinks, company, and a few strange stories from around the valley.
story.prologue.saloon.abigail.1: There's no shortage of strange things here. Once I stayed near the graveyard too late and heard something right behind me... but nobody was there.
story.prologue.saloon.pam.1: Hmph. Keep telling yourself that. Some things are better not called out too loudly, especially at night.
story.prologue.saloon.farmer.prompt: Everyone looks toward you. Instead of lowering your voice, you laugh it off.
story.prologue.saloon.choice.never: Haha! You must all be seeing things. Ghosts? Come on, none of that is real!
story.prologue.saloon.choice.doubt: If ghosts are real, tell one to come find me. I'd like to see what it can do.
story.prologue.saloon.gus.warning: Hey... I wouldn't sound so certain. There are a few things in this valley that seem more interested in people who dismiss them.
story.prologue.saloon.abigail.warning: Exactly. You don't mess around with the supernatural.
story.prologue.saloon.narration.wizard: Outside the window, a purple-robed figure passing by suddenly stops. It seems he heard that last part.
story.prologue.saloon.wizard.1: Hm... never encountered it, have you? Then perhaps I should show you.
story.prologue.saloon.narration.end: When you look outside again, the road is empty.^Conversation in the saloon continues as if nothing happened... but that remark stays in your head.
story.prologue.saloon.after: You leave the Stardrop Saloon with a strangely uneasy feeling...
story.wizard7.narration.1: That morning, someone knocks at the door. When you open it, the Wizard is standing there as though he knew exactly when you'd answer.
story.wizard7.line.1: Seven days. Have you learned your lesson?
story.wizard7.line.2: That night at the saloon... I heard every word you said.
story.wizard7.line.3: I sent the tape that appeared outside your door. I merely wanted you to understand that things on the other side do not require your belief in order to exist.
story.wizard7.line.4: Hm. Whatever your answer, you're still in one piece. That's already a fairly good outcome.
story.wizard7.line.5: I suspect... you've grown somewhat attached to that ghost too, haven't you?
story.wizard7.line.6: I'm giving you a cabinet. An Occult Cabinet. If you decide to test your luck with something else someday, use it to temporarily seal the anchor of whatever is attached to you.
story.wizard7.narration.cabinet: The Wizard sets down a dark wooden cabinet. Pale purple symbols are carved across its door.
story.wizard7.line.final: Only let one thing attach itself to you at a time. I have no desire to collect the pieces of your soul. You do not mess around with the supernatural.
cabinet.menu.title: Occult Cabinet
cabinet.menu.intro.active: The cabinet hums softly. The Cursed VHS is still linking Sudoku to the farmhouse.
cabinet.menu.intro.sealed: The air around the cabinet is icy. The Cursed VHS is sealed inside.
cabinet.sudoku.seal.low.1: ‘You want to put me back in there?’
cabinet.sudoku.seal.mid.1: ‘You want me to go back into the tape?’
cabinet.sudoku.seal.high.2: ‘I understand. But... don't leave me in there too long.’
cabinet.sudoku.seal.question: Are you sure you want to seal this connection?
cabinet.sudoku.sealed: The Cursed VHS has been sealed. The farmhouse suddenly feels uncomfortably quiet.
cabinet.unseal.blocked: Another haunting is still active. Seal it first.
cabinet.sudoku.return.mid: ‘I'm back. You still haven't learned to leave cursed things alone, have you?’
cabinet.sudoku.return.high: ‘...You finally remembered I was still in the cabinet.’
cabinet.sudoku.return.question: Sudoku looks at you, then glances toward the Occult Cabinet.
cabinet.sudoku.return.progress: Connection restored • progress and Trust preserved.
spiriteve.none: Sudoku hasn't made a Spirit's Eve plan with you this year.
spiriteve.plan.1: "Tonight the living pretend to be ghosts?"
spiriteve.plan.3: Sudoku tilts her head. "Am I allowed to scare them?"
spiriteve.question: What do you tell Sudoku?
spiriteve.response.free.2: "...I'll try not to make anyone run too far."
spiriteve.response.lewis.1: Sudoku is silent for a few seconds.
spiriteve.response.gentle.2: Sudoku tries to smile. It does not make her any less frightening.
spiriteve.progress: Spirit's Eve • Sudoku will appear at the festival tonight
spiriteve.aftermath.free.1: "Living people scream very loudly when frightened."
spiriteve.aftermath.free.2: Sudoku is quiet for a moment. "...Can I go again next year?"
spiriteve.aftermath.lewis.1: "Lewis avoided me until the festival ended."
spiriteve.aftermath.lewis.2: "...I think he stayed conscious. Can I go again next year?"
spiriteve.aftermath.gentle.2: Sudoku looks away. "...Can I go again next year?"
spiriteve.festival.sudoku.free: ...They really pay to pretend to be ghosts?$1#$e#I scared three people. Abigail wants me to do it again.$3
spiriteve.festival.sudoku.lewis: Lewis is avoiding me.$4#$e#I don't understand. You only told me not to make him faint.$1
spiriteve.festival.sudoku.gentle: ...I'm scaring them very gently.$4#$e#Abigail said I have a nice 'costume.' I haven't corrected her.$1
spiriteve.festival.abigail: That girl with you has an amazing scary costume! ...Wait, is that not a costume?$1
spiriteve.festival.sebastian: Sudoku doesn't talk much. I kind of like that.$0
spiriteve.festival.wizard: Your new companion does not belong wholly to our realm. I suspect you already know that.$0
spiriteve.festival.krobus: Your dark-haired friend is very quiet. I like her.$1
spiriteve.festival.lewis.free: That girl with you appeared behind me three times. Three times, @!$2
spiriteve.festival.lewis.lewis: @... please tell your friend that silently standing behind the mayor is not a festival activity.$2
spiriteve.festival.lewis.gentle: Your friend has... a very convincing festival spirit. Very, very convincing.$2
gift.already.1: Sudoku glances at the item in your hand.
gift.already.2: “You already gave me something today. Do living people exchange gifts this often?”
gift.empty.1: Sudoku looks at your empty hands.
gift.empty.2: “...Were you planning to give me air?”
gift.invalid.1: Sudoku studies the item, then shakes her head.
gift.invalid.2: “That should stay where it belongs. Don't give it to me.”
gift.offer.question: Give {{item}} to Sudoku?
gift.pencil.1: Sudoku freezes for a moment when she sees the pencil.
gift.pencil.2: “...Another pencil? I still remember the first one.”
gift.loved.1: Sudoku accepts {{item}} with both hands, quiet longer than usual.
gift.liked.1: Sudoku looks over {{item}}, then gives a small nod.
gift.liked.2: “I like this. ...Don't look so pleased with yourself.”
gift.neutral.1: Sudoku accepts {{item}} and studies it for a while.
gift.neutral.2: “I still don't understand what living people expect me to do with gifts... but I'll keep it.”
gift.disliked.1: Sudoku looks at {{item}}, then stares at you for a long moment.
gift.disliked.2: “...You do know I can't eat, right?”
gift.hated.1: Sudoku holds {{item}} between two fingers like evidence from a crime scene.
gift.hated.2: “If this is how living people show affection... I'm starting to understand why there are so many ghosts.”
sudoku.help.title: How to Play Sudoku
sudoku.help.goal: Goal: fill every empty cell. Use 1–9 once in each row, column, and 3×3 box.
sudoku.help.rule.box: 3. Box: no repeats inside a 3×3 box.
sudoku.help.example: Only 5 can go in the blue cell.
sudoku.help.tip: Tip: start with a row, column, or box missing only one number. You never need to guess.
sudoku.help.legend: White = fixed clue  •  Blue = your entry.
sudoku.help.controls: Select an empty cell, choose 1–9, then Check. Hint fills one unresolved cell: Easy 3, Normal 2, Hard 1.
rescue.line: ...I haven't given you permission to die.
capstone.title: CHANNEL 18 — SUDOKU
capstone.1: The TV turns on by itself. The plug is still on the floor.
capstone.2: The faded 18 on the VHS label becomes clear through the static.
capstone.3: “I carried eighteen unfinished grids when I was pulled through the screen.”
capstone.4: “I thought solving the last one would make me disappear.”
capstone.6: “Because you kept coming back. I think I started waiting for you.”
capstone.6.stay: “Because you kept coming back. If you truly want that... I will stay.”
capstone.6.home: Sudoku looks around the room. “...My home. I never thought I would have a place like that again.”
capstone.7: The signal settles on channel 18. Sudoku is no longer only a haunting.
capstone.after: Sudoku sits beside the TV. “...One more puzzle tomorrow?”
capstone.after.stay: Sudoku sits beside the TV. “...I will stay. One more puzzle tomorrow?”
capstone.after.home: Sudoku sits beside the TV and looks around the room. “...One more puzzle at home tomorrow?”
capstone.status.complete: Channel 18 is stable • Sudoku's case is complete
channel18.title: CHANNEL 18 — STABLE SIGNAL
channel18.progress: Sudoku's case is complete. The signal remains.
channel18.tv.line: The screen shivers. Between the ordinary channels, a band of static marked 18 appears.
channel18.tv.question: What do you want to watch?
channel18.broadcast.question: The signal waits for your choice.
channel18.choice.stay: Beneath the static, Sudoku repeats, “You told me to stay.”
channel18.choice.home: The screen reflects the room. Sudoku says quietly, “Our home is still in one piece.”
channel18.broadcast.spring.0.a: The rain is loud against the farmhouse roof.
channel18.broadcast.spring.0.b: Good. It makes the empty cells easier to hear.
channel18.broadcast.spring.1.b: “You stayed. That part is not seasonal.”
channel18.broadcast.summer.0.a: The TV glass is warm tonight.
channel18.broadcast.summer.0.b: “Do not touch it. I am using the heat.”
channel18.broadcast.summer.1.b: “I can tell which one is lying.”
channel18.broadcast.fall.0.a: The static sounds almost like leaves.
channel18.broadcast.fall.0.b: “Almost. The TV is worse at being a tree.”
channel18.broadcast.winter.0.a: The farmhouse is quiet under the snow.
channel18.broadcast.winter.0.b: “Quiet is not the same as empty.”
channel18.broadcast.winter.1.a: The screen reflected you before you walked in.
epilogue.line.1: Seven days have passed since Channel 18 stabilized.
epilogue.line.2: The TV turns on without any static. Sudoku has set out a new grid and sharpened two pencils.
epilogue.line.stay: “You told me to stay. I wanted to know whether you still meant it on the seventh day.”
epilogue.line.home: “You called this my home. I wanted to try something living people do at home.”
epilogue.question: Will you sit beside her?
epilogue.after: Sudoku slides one pencil toward you. “...Do not get the first cell wrong.”
spiriteve.scene.title: SPIRIT'S EVE — CHANNEL 18
spiriteve.scene.gentle.1: The festival lanterns dim for one breath.
spiriteve.scene.gentle.2: The TV-static sound follows Sudoku into the crowd.
spiriteve.scene.gentle.3: She appears behind the masks, perfectly still.
spiriteve.scene.gentle.4: A few villagers turn around at once. Sudoku waves.
spiriteve.scene.gentle.5: “I am being gentle. This is gentle.”
spiriteve.scene.gentle.6: By the time the lanterns brighten, nobody can agree what they saw.
spiriteve.scene.free.1: Sudoku steps into the festival lights.
spiriteve.scene.free.2: Every lantern goes dark except the one above her.
spiriteve.scene.free.3: Three afterimages cross the square in different directions.
spiriteve.scene.free.4: The crowd scatters. Abigail looks delighted.
spiriteve.scene.free.5: “They said I should do it again next year.”
spiriteve.scene.free.6: The static stops. Somewhere, a laugh comes from the TV.
spiriteve.scene.lewis.1: Lewis checks the festival gate twice.
spiriteve.scene.lewis.3: He turns. She is gone. He turns back. She is closer.
spiriteve.scene.lewis.4: Lewis makes a sound that he will later deny.
spiriteve.scene.lewis.5: Sudoku whispers, “You told me not to make you faint.”
spiriteve.scene.lewis.6: The festival continues. Lewis does not look behind him again.

daily.0.0.b: Don't stare at me like that. Look at the puzzle.
daily.0.1.a: I heard your footsteps from the other side of the screen.
daily.0.1.b: If you're playing, don't make too many mistakes. The sound of erasing is irritating.
daily.0.2.a: I'm not crawling out of the TV again today.
daily.0.3.b: I thought this house would drive you away before it managed to get rid of me.
daily.0.4.b: And don't touch the cells that already have numbers. Both are irritating.
daily.1.0.b: At least I don't have to call you through the TV.
daily.1.0.q: Will you stay with me for a while today?
daily.1.1.b: Don't get smug. I only said acceptable.
daily.1.1.q: What do you want to do next?
daily.1.2.b: It's not hard enough to run away from. Probably.
daily.1.2.q: What do you want to do today?
daily.1.3.a: You're starting to give me fewer headaches.
daily.1.3.q: What do you want to do today?
daily.1.4.a: Yesterday you did better than I expected.
daily.2.0.a: I saved this puzzle for you.
daily.2.0.b: Don't make me regret choosing it.
daily.2.1.a: You came home later than yesterday.
daily.2.1.b: I... only noticed. The clock in here is loud.
daily.2.1.q: Sit with me for a while?
daily.2.2.b: This puzzle suits you better than the earlier ones. I chose it a little more carefully.
daily.2.2.q: What do you want to do with me?
daily.2.3.b: Maybe I should find harder puzzles before you start getting pleased with yourself.
daily.2.4.a: The house was too quiet today.
daily.2.4.b: Good thing you're home. ...I mean the noise, that's all.
daily.2.4.q: Sit with me for a while?
daily.3.0.b: ...Good. I was starting to think this room was too quiet.
daily.3.0.q: Will you stay with me today?
daily.3.1.b: Not exactly because I missed you. The house was just quiet... though it wasn't entirely not because I missed you.
daily.3.2.a: I'm starting to understand why living people like small routines.
daily.3.2.b: You come home, I give you a puzzle, the house makes noise again. Repeating it... is rather pleasant.
daily.3.2.q: Sit with me for a while?
daily.3.3.a: I kept this spot for you.
daily.3.3.b: Don't make me say out loud that I like having someone sit with me.
daily.3.4.a: I picked a puzzle that's just difficult enough.
daily.3.4.b: I want to see how much further you've improved... before I have to find something nastier.
daily.3.4.q: What do you want to do with me today?
daily.4.0.b: You solved everything I brought with me... and you still came back.
daily.4.0.q: Will you still stay with me today?
daily.4.1.a: I don't have any more Stages to use as an excuse to keep you here.
daily.4.1.b: ...I can find more puzzles. Or perhaps we don't need one.
daily.4.2.a: Perhaps I've run out of reasons to make you stay.
daily.4.2.b: Good thing you don't seem to need a reason anymore.
daily.4.2.q: Stay with me for a while?
daily.disabled.question: Sudoku looks away.
daily.repeat.0.q: Want to stay a little longer?
daily.repeat.1.q: Anything else you want to do?
daily.repeat.2.a: I still have the puzzle here.
daily.solved.question.close: Do you still want to stay with me a little longer today?
daily.solved.question.early: Want to stay a little longer?
hub.opening: Sudoku watches you, waiting for you to speak.
hub.question: ...What do you want to do today?
hub.trust.already: Trust {{trust}}/30 • you've already spent time talking together today.
intro.0.line1: Sudoku stares at you without blinking.
intro.0.question: How do you answer?
intro.pencil.normal.1: Sudoku is silent for a few seconds.
intro.pencil.question: What do you give her?
intro.pencil.tv.2: Sudoku glances at the TV. "...It is easier to understand than you."

roommate.activity-label.wait: Waiting for you to come home
roommate.activity.corner.0.b: From here I can hear the wood creak, the fire crackle... and even when you walk past.
roommate.activity.corner.1.b: This corner simply gets less traffic. A little quiet makes the thoughts in my head less tangled.
roommate.activity.corner.2.b: Living people sometimes sit perfectly still and do nothing too, don't they? I'm trying it.
roommate.activity.door.0.b: I can tell you're coming home while your footsteps are still far away, before your hand ever reaches the knob.
roommate.activity.door.1.b: In, out, close, open... very orderly. Very principled.
roommate.activity.door.2.a: I'm only standing here for a little while.
roommate.activity.door.2.b: ...I'm not waiting for you. It just means I'll know first if you happen to come home.
roommate.activity.furniture.0.b: Living people own an impressive number of things whose only purpose is to hold other things. It's confusing.
roommate.activity.furniture.2.a: I'm watching the house change little by little.
roommate.activity.furniture.2.b: You drag things around all day, clattering everywhere... and by night it's a different house again.
roommate.activity.listen.0.b: During the day it clicks and murmurs softly. At night, every settling board becomes much clearer.
roommate.activity.listen.1.a: There are tiny, regular clicks inside the walls.
roommate.activity.listen.1.b: Usually I reach seventy-three before you open the door. Today I only reached seventy-one.
roommate.activity.listen.2.a: The house sounds different when you're here.
roommate.activity.listen.2.b: Not exactly louder. The noises have more rhythm, as though the house knows someone is living inside it.
roommate.activity.pet.0.b: I think it knew I was here long before you finally looked straight at me.
roommate.activity.pet.1.a: This animal isn't afraid of me at all.
roommate.activity.pet.1.b: ...I still haven't decided whether that's a compliment or a tiny insult.
roommate.activity.pet.2.a: Its eyes keep following me, slowly from one side to the other.
roommate.activity.pet.2.b: Perhaps it likes me more than you. I'm only considering the possibility.
roommate.activity.tv.0.b: When it's off, the room reflects faintly in the glass. It almost looks like a doorway.
roommate.activity.tv.1.a: The TV crackled with static when you walked in.
roommate.activity.tv.1.b: That wasn't me. ...At least not this time.
roommate.activity.tv.2.b: It reflects the house rather clearly. You too... even while you keep pacing around.
roommate.activity.wait.0.a: I'm waiting for you to come home.
roommate.activity.wait.0.b: ...Yes. Waiting. There's no need to rename it to make it less awkward.
roommate.activity.wait.1.a: I've kept the spot beside me empty.
roommate.activity.wait.1.b: No special reason. It's just... if you come home, I won't have to make room.
roommate.activity.wait.2.a: I was going to pick out a puzzle for you.
roommate.activity.wait.2.b: Then I remembered we don't actually need to solve anything just to sit together.
roommate.strange.0.a: The TV flashed a frame I've never seen before.
roommate.strange.0.b: Just a pitch-black hallway and a half-open door. I turned it off before anything could step through.
roommate.strange.1.a: Something was standing outside the door earlier.
roommate.strange.1.b: Tall, perfectly still. I looked away for a moment, and when I looked back it was gone.
roommate.strange.2.a: The mirror in the house is reflecting you one beat late.
roommate.strange.2.b: Only one beat. ...Don't stand in front of it too long today.
roommate.strange.3.a: The animal keeps staring over your shoulder.
roommate.strange.3.b: I'm not standing there. And I don't intend to turn around and check what is.
roommate.strange.4.a: Last night there was a knock... knock... from inside the TV.
roommate.strange.4.b: Three knocks, a pause, then three more. I didn't answer.
roommate.talk.0.0.b: I don't have anything special to say. But if you want to sit there for a while... sit.
roommate.talk.0.1.a: Living people really do talk a lot.
roommate.talk.0.1.b: You, though... you're only loud enough to be tolerable.
roommate.talk.0.2.b: I haven't asked why you grow an entire field of turnips as though your life depends on it.
roommate.talk.0.3.a: No puzzle, and you're still standing here?
roommate.talk.0.3.b: ...You're strange in a very living-person sort of way.
roommate.talk.1.0.b: I only noticed. Don't read too much into it.
roommate.talk.1.1.a: I'm starting to recognize your footsteps.
roommate.talk.1.1.b: Quick at first, then slower just before the door. Easy to recognize.
roommate.talk.1.2.a: You have a very strange habit.
roommate.talk.1.2.b: You come back every day to talk to a ghost, and act as though that's perfectly normal.
roommate.talk.1.3.a: This house isn't as quiet as it used to be.
roommate.talk.1.3.b: Doors, footsteps, furniture clattering... strangely, I don't hate it.
roommate.talk.2.0.a: I was going to tell you something.
roommate.talk.2.0.b: ...Then the thought drifted away. Ask tomorrow. Maybe it'll come back.
roommate.talk.2.1.b: You don't have to tell me everything. Pick one thing... I'll listen.
roommate.talk.2.2.a: I think I've gotten used to the sound of the door when you come home.
roommate.talk.2.2.b: Don't replace it. That creak... is easy to recognize.
roommate.talk.2.3.a: You don't have to bring out a puzzle every time.
roommate.talk.2.3.b: Some days, sitting quietly for a while is enough. I won't keep score.
roommate.talk.3.0.b: ...Good. The house was quieter than it needed to be.
roommate.talk.3.1.a: I like the days when you stay home longer.
roommate.talk.3.1.b: Wait. Pretend you didn't hear that.
roommate.talk.3.2.a: Maybe living people call this... familiarity.
roommate.talk.3.2.b: Something repeats and repeats, until one day its absence feels empty.
roommate.talk.3.3.a: If one day I'm not standing by the TV anymore...
roommate.talk.3.3.b: You'd still come looking for me, wouldn't you? ...You don't have to answer now.
roommate.talk.4.0.a: I don't need Sudoku to keep you sitting here anymore, do I?
roommate.talk.4.0.b: ...Good. I was getting tired of pretending that was the reason.
roommate.talk.4.1.b: I'm not denying it this time. Denying things gets tiring.
roommate.talk.4.2.a: This house used to be yours alone.
roommate.talk.4.2.b: Now... there are a few corners that feel familiar enough to be mine too.
roommate.talk.4.3.a: We don't have to play today.
roommate.talk.4.3.b: I only wanted to know you made it home. That's enough.
roommate.welcome.0.0: Sudoku turns her head slightly. "...You're home."
roommate.welcome.0.1: Sudoku looks toward the door. "I heard your footsteps from outside."
roommate.welcome.1.0: Sudoku watches you for a moment. "You came home later than usual today."
roommate.welcome.1.1: "...You're home." Sudoku gives a small nod and returns to what she was doing.
roommate.welcome.2.0: Sudoku tilts her head slightly. "You're home. ...Good."
roommate.welcome.2.1: "I knew you'd come back." Sudoku says it as though it were obvious.
roommate.welcome.3.0: "You're home." Sudoku's shoulders relax, just slightly.
roommate.welcome.3.1: Sudoku looks over at you. "I waited for you." This time she doesn't add anything to take it back.
